teaser.text: Techtronic Industries Company Limited, usually called TTI, makes branded tools, outdoor equipment and cleaning machines. Its business is simple to describe but revealing to follow: products move from factories to retailers, while money moves back through a chain of customers, suppliers and operating costs.

blocks.heading: Where could TTI's shares be by 2029?

paragraphs.text: The October 2029 range is HK$91.69 to HK$226.47. Today’s price is HK$130.60. The base case has the highest probability at 54%. The bear case has 28%. The bull case has 18%.

blocks.heading: What has to go right for TTI's forecast?

paragraphs.text: The bear assumes weaker reorders, slower factory transfers and falling normalized margins. The bull requires Milwaukee gains, stronger Ryobi repeat buying and smooth transfers. First-half 2026 net income rose to US$738.407m, while Milwaukee’s underlying growth was 10.5%, supporting continued progress but not guaranteeing the bull outcome.

blocks.heading: How much cash does TTI really make?

paragraphs.text: TTI’s own count was US$1,395 million because it excludes lease payments and includes equipment-disposal proceeds. A more conservative view subtracts US$39.31 million of share-based compensation. That is not a current cash payment, but it recognizes the cost of dilution borne by shareholders.

blocks.heading: What does an investor pay for TTI today?

paragraphs.text: The price-to-earnings ratio, or P/E, compares the share price with annual earnings per share. TTI’s trailing P/E uses the last twelve months of reported earnings, while its forward P/E uses an estimate. The two multiples imply earnings of about HK$5.61 and HK$7.22 per share respectively, an increase of roughly 29%. That is an expectation, not a guarantee: Milwaukee growth, margins, financing costs, taxes and buybacks may all differ from the forecast.

dividend.closing: The full memo also explains TTI’s business, rivals, management, and risks.

blocks.heading: How much does TTI pay per share?

paragraphs.text: Base dividends per share increase from US$0.42 in October 2027 to US$0.50 in October 2029. The bear reaches US$0.39, while the bull reaches US$0.60. The declared 2026 interim dividend rose 20%, but competing demands from investment and buybacks argue for moderation.

blocks.heading: Is TTI’s dividend covered by its cash?

paragraphs.text: Dividends were US$572.651 million in 2025. Repurchases were US$41.728 million. Together they consumed 50.1% of free cash flow, so TTI still retained substantial cash for strengthening the balance sheet.

Free cash flow is cash left after operating needs and investment. The broader 2025 calculation deducts US$589.865 million for equipment and intangible additions. It also deducts US$161.822 million of lease payments, leaving US$1,227.494 million.

paragraphs.text: The dividend probabilities are 55% for base, 25% for bear and 20% for bull. TTI’s five-year record was flat or rising, but it has no formal dividend-growth target.
The base case gains support if Milwaukee and the core brands sustain growth through 2027, margins move toward 10.0% and free cash flow funds investment, dividends and buybacks.
